idiom_name: actor-guarded free list with async acquire/release
implementation_notes: Swift ships no pool type, so the structure is hand-written - but the idiomatic shape is an actor rather than a locked class: keep idle instances in an actor-isolated array and expose `func acquire() async -> T` / `func release(_:)`, letting actor isolation serialise access instead of a DispatchQueue or os_unfair_lock. SE-0306 defines the rules that matter here: cross-actor calls are asynchronous, their argument and result types must be Sendable, and actors are reentrant - every await inside acquire() is a suspension point where another task can consume the state you just inspected, so pool state must be re-checked after each await. When the pool must wait for a free instance, the actor stores CheckedContinuation values in a waiter queue and resumes them from release().
pitfalls: Actor reentrancy: an await between inspecting the free list and handing out an instance lets another task take it first, so re-validate state after every suspension point.
Cross-actor acquire/release requires the pooled type to be Sendable; mutable reference types will not compile, and an @unchecked Sendable wrapper hands the race back to you.
Suspending checkout needs continuations: without a waiter queue an exhausted pool must fail or allocate outside its bound, and resuming a continuation twice crashes the process.
